items.title: M2: Capture branded tracked values and current semantic observations
items.body:
## Problem and scope

Production Tracking currently captures process-local tags only. M2 requires ordinary object reads and function calls to produce portable semantic evidence while retaining isolated capture and reactive composition.

Governing contracts: TRK-1 through TRK-8, VAL-1/2/3, ARC-001 through ARC-004, A-01/A-04/A-15/A-18. Depends on #24. This issue remains backlog until Value declarations are accepted and the supervisor records the bounded object-ownership/update and alpha API contracts here.

## Intended behavior and ownership

- Transparent nominally branded `tracked()` supports the selected plain-object/array domain and normal function invocation, rejects primitive wrapper inputs in types and runtime, and allows importing a tracked declaration without rewrapping at each consumer.
- Tracking captures operations and compares supplied current facts. Definition/composition supplies current binding correspondence; Tracking must not derive restart identity from function text, labels, object identity, or invocation order. Any binding descriptor supplied to Tracking is copied/validated and treated as caller-owned correspondence information, not a Tracking registry's proof of identity.
- Called tracked functions contribute automatic actual-called implementation evidence and internal tracked reads/calls, but are not memoized merely by wrapping. Uncalled functions contribute no code dependency. Document emitted-build-artifact invalidation policy and closure limits. Use the injected hash/async-context capabilities without direct Node access.
- Capture sync/async operations in isolated frames, restore surrounding context on success/throw/rejection, fail clearly on detached late use, and replay observations through cached local derivations. Keep tag/revision/frame state process-local; only immutable versioned semantic evidence leaves the persistence-facing seam.
- Controlled state changes and ownership must prevent a cached derivation from silently reusing evidence after an unobservable mutation. The supervisor will record the concrete minimal contract before implementation; do not silently choose raw mutable inputs with unverifiable cache validity.

## Tests first and acceptance

1. Jest and tsd failures before implementation: supported wrappers and primitive/class rejection, nominal brand and normal call/return typing, imported declarations, and intentional alpha/default-public declaration boundaries.
2. TRK-5 local supported operations: leaf reads without whole-object/identity inflation; missing vs present-undefined; actual falsey guard values; own versus inherited presence; key enumeration/order without member payload reads; array length and positional paths; explicit identity-field reads; pass-through argument reads only as consumed by the callee. Reflection must preserve Proxy invariants and must not accidentally record stronger dependencies than the performed operation.
3. Actual-called implementation evidence, uncalled helper exclusion, repeated calls execute repeatedly, tracked nested/async function reads, and bounded unsupported function/native behavior with diagnostics.
4. Changed branch replaces abandoned reads; concurrent frames remain isolated; nested throw/rejection restores parent; detached work after close rejects; cached derived success/failure replays relevant semantic evidence without storing tags.
5. A-04 M2 slice uses an injected current-fact/binding provider: replace author A with B keeping the name equal, then change B's name. First selected-fact comparison equals, second changes; original observation snapshot remains immutable. Missing/ambiguous correspondence yields an explicit non-equal/unavailable result, never guessed remapping. Durable accepted result references and persisted provenance remain M3.
6. Selected output/pass-through materialization integrates through an observation contract with the dependent M2 materialization issue; no returned tracked object can be treated as a fully observed immutable snapshot merely because it crossed a function boundary.
7. Tests and generated declarations demonstrate immutable serializable evidence with no live tags, revisions, closures, or mutable source objects. Required check/test/build and import/declaration boundaries pass.

## Delivery and exclusions

One isolated worktree and issue claim; accurate PR template with test-first evidence and `Refs #N`; stop at PR-open. No History writes, reuse eligibility/source policy, graph mutation or general fanout. No claim of arbitrary JavaScript closure soundness. Normative changes require supervisor review. The materialization issue number in this draft will be resolved by the supervisor before pickup.

items.title: M2: Enforce the supported tracked-capture boundary with typed lint
items.body:
## Purpose and dependencies

Add the bounded compiler-informed capture check required by TRK-4. Depends on the accepted wrapper/brand contract in #26. This is a correctness aid for supported syntax, not a proof of arbitrary JavaScript closure soundness.

## Contract

Use TypeScript checker information and existing lexical-scope services with the actual shared tracked brand. Recognize the approved tracked function entrypoints through resolved symbols/types rather than spelling alone. Diagnose untracked external influences captured by supported tracked function declarations, including a scalar extracted from tracked configuration before the active computation, external branch selectors, and untracked helper calls. Local variables and parameters do not all need brands. Imported branded objects/functions remain valid across generated package declarations.

Document the exact supported declaration/call syntax, builtin exemption policy, unsupported dynamic constructs, and deliberate policy/suppression boundary. No semantic-changing autofix. Do not label missed dynamic/aliased cases as soundly checked. Existing strict type-aware lint, suppression policy and architecture checks remain in force.

## Acceptance: tests first

- Real TypeScript-program positive and negative fixtures precede implementation and fail for expected capture diagnostics.
- Positive: supported locals/parameters, actual branded imported config/helper, tracked branch read inside computation, documented builtins.
- Negative: untracked captured scalar, extracted scalar before frame, external branch guard, untracked function/helper, fake structural brand, shadowed or same-spelled nonframework helper where relevant to rule identification.
- Generated alpha/public declaration-consumer behavior follows #26 release tiers. No raw sibling source aliases or mocked checker substitutions.
- Missing type information fails clearly for the checked supported surface. Rule enabled in normal check path; negative gate-omission fixture detects disabling/skipping it.
- Run focused tests plus `npm run check`, `npm test`, `npm run build`; report initial RED and exact successful commands/limits.

One isolated worktree/claim, stop at PR-open with `Refs #N` and accurate attribution. Owner: tooling enforcing Tracking's TRK-4 contract. No runtime memoization or speculative purity analysis.

items.title: Presence checks on supported plain records reject intrinsic property names
items.body:
## Problem and governing contract

**Medium correctness: valid presence operations are rejected.** On a supported ordinary `{}`, own-presence checks for `constructor`, `__proto__`, `toString`, and `hasOwnProperty` should return false; inherited membership should return true. Both currently throw `Unsupported value ... intrinsic inherited data`. Ordinary tracked `'constructor' in input` fails too.

TRK-5 in [tracking.md](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/blob/c5802daca4a0bb8ea91159854d84eddcfa5215b6/docs/spec/tracking.md#observation-decision-table) says own checks consume ownership only and `in` consumes presence, neither the value at that key. The selected Value domain permits plain-data prototype chains ending in `Object.prototype` and rejects selected intrinsic **values**. This reproduction requests presence, so no native function/accessor serialization is needed.

The cause is `observeAt` calling `lookupValidated` before branching on own/membership/value in `packages/value/src/value.ts`. The intrinsic-value restriction is applied even when only a boolean fact is consumed. This is distinct from #155's omitted container-guard dependency.

## Test-first reproduction

Branch `gap-hunt-contracts`, fixed reproduction commit [`9267a44e1a203966e6ccd73db188e5826506326b`](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/commit/9267a44e1a203966e6ccd73db188e5826506326b), baseline `c5802daca4a0bb8ea91159854d84eddcfa5215b6`.

From a clean checkout of that revision with Node24 and npm:

```sh
node scratch/gap-hunt/contracts/reproduce.mjs intrinsic
```

The runner installs locked dependencies, builds generated declarations, compiles and runs [the focused fixture](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/blob/9267a44e1a203966e6ccd73db188e5826506326b/packages/tracking/test/gap-hunt-contracts-intrinsic-presence.test.ts). No local absolute paths, existing stores or paid services are required. Linux execution is pending the owner's devbox; the command uses portable Node/npm entrypoints.

Observed: **9 failed, 2 passed**, independently rerun by the supervising agent on Node24.22.1/macOS. All eight special-name own/membership assertions and ordinary tracked membership fail. Selected intrinsic-value rejection and supported shadowing/custom plain-data prototype controls pass. Strict TypeScript and type-aware lint pass. The script propagates the red suite's nonzero status.

## Implementation handoff

Pickup-ready within the existing supported domain. Queue priority follows #155's silent false reuse and precedes DX/docs. Start by retaining the observed failing presence assertions.

## Numbered acceptance criteria

1. For a supported ordinary `{}`, own-presence of `constructor`, `__proto__`,
   `toString`, and `hasOwnProperty` returns false; inherited membership returns
   true. Both operations record only their boolean semantic fact and structured
   address, without evaluating or encoding the intrinsic member's value.
2. Ordinary tracked `'constructor' in input` succeeds and records one membership
   observation. The owning explicit own-property helper agrees with Value's own
   observation. Do not implement membership as an own-only check.
3. Transition an own supported data property to inherited intrinsic presence:
   own-presence changes true→false, while inherited membership remains true.
   Unrelated sibling edits do not alter those facts; deletion under a null-ending
   chain produces the actual absent membership result.
4. Selected intrinsic **value** reads continue to reject explicitly; this issue
   must not add native function/accessor data support. Preserve rejection of user
   accessors without invoking them, unsupported class/native prototypes, and
   prototype-depth violations. Preserve supported custom plain-data prototypes
   and own-data shadowing of intrinsic names.
5. Assertions cover Value and Tracking, include positive/negative controls,
   and pass strict TypeScript and type-aware lint. Add current-fact comparison
   or assembled durable acceptance coverage so this is not merely a direct lookup
   special case. No discarded or fabricated dependency fact is acceptable.

Scope: operation-specific presence semantics within the already selected supported
plain-data prototype domain. Out of scope: #155 container evidence, arbitrary
prototype/native data support, native reflection as an alternative observation
API, provider work or publication. No design-policy expansion is required.


Dependencies: no blocking issue. Coordinate shared Value/Tracking edits with #155 if concurrently claimed, but this reproduction and correction do not depend on its resolution.

## Attribution

Implementer: Codex worker (`gpt-6.1-sol`), operating for Mike North.
Agent assistance: The worker authored the synthetic reproduction and contract. The supervising Codex agent inspected TRK-5 and the supported prototype boundary, independently reran the 9-red/2-green fixture, checked live issues/PRs/labels, and filed this finding. No human implementation or review is claimed. No production fix is included.

items.title: EXP-6: Pilot a Lean proof for bounded value observations
items.body:
## Problem
A small formal model may reveal mistakes in normalization or projection meaning, but only if its assumptions and maintenance cost are explicit. Test one theorem after #6 fixes the bounded value domain.

## Governing sources
- [M1 experiments](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/blob/main/docs/milestones.md#m1--bounded-contract-and-architecture-experiments)
- [EXP-0 evidence contract](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/blob/main/docs/spec/experiments.md#common-experiment-contract)
- [EXP-6 charter](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/blob/main/docs/spec/experiments.md#exp-6--lean-semantic-pilot)
- [TRK-5 observations](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/blob/main/docs/spec/tracking.md#observation-decision-table)
- [VAL-1 paths](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/blob/main/docs/spec/tracking.md#structured-addresses-and-fingerprints)

## Acceptance criteria (write assertions first)
1. State one independent theorem and its bounded value algebra before writing proof code; include valid TRK-5/VAL-1/2 examples and counterexamples that would falsify an incorrect theorem.
2. Check the theorem with no sorry or unreviewed new axiom; list assumptions, including hash collision resistance as an assumption rather than equality.
3. If a TypeScript comparison oracle is practical, compare independently generated cases with #6; report mismatches without copying production branches.
4. Give a pass/reject/inconclusive adoption recommendation and reproducible toolchain, trust boundary, and maintenance estimate.

## Non-goals
No proof of the full runtime, paid-work determinism, mandatory Lean CI for unrelated contexts, or claim that model proof establishes TypeScript correctness.

## Evidence to provide
Proof source, checker output, counterexample fixture, explicit assumptions, and decision record.

**Dependencies:** #6. **Readiness:** backlog until #6 establishes the bounded domain.

items.title: M2: Establish production value semantics and injected SHA-256
items.body:
## Problem and scope

M2 needs production canonical values and structured addresses before Tracking can capture portable semantic evidence. EXP-2 selected a bounded mechanism, but production packages cannot import experiment source. Establish `@microdelta/value` as the strong supporting component in ARC-002; preserve the six context owners.

Governing contracts: VAL-1/2/3, TRK-5 literal fact semantics, ARC-002/010, PKG-001 through PKG-008, TEST-1, A-15/A-20. M0.5 and M1 prerequisites are accepted. This issue is ready independently of the remaining M2 work.

## Implementation boundaries

- Own canonical equality encoding, snapshot transport, structured property/index addresses, validation of selected facts, and SHA-256 fingerprints in `@microdelta/value`. Tracking will own capture/observation records and the decision of which fact was consumed. Do not add binding correspondence, reuse eligibility, collection traversal policy, or persistence.
- Promote the selected EXP-2 supported domain and MDV1/MDS1/MDO1 mechanisms into independently tested production modules; no runtime import from experiments. Unknown/malformed/noncanonical versions fail closed; these formats do not migrate existing History rows.
- Host hashing is an injected synchronous capability defined by Machine and implemented with Node crypto in `machine-node`. Value owns canonical input and digest meaning; Machine owns only the SHA-256 operation. Add the necessary Value-to-Machine supporting edge explicitly and prove portable compilation plus A-20. No other host capability is authorized by this issue.
- Cross-package contracts are alpha, intentional release tags/TSDoc, generated declaration consumers, real runtime exports, and no private source aliases. Register the package in build order, declaration preflight and gate wiring; test omissions so a new package cannot silently evade the foundation checks. Keep existing facade public exports compatible.

## Tests first and acceptance

1. Before implementation, write Jest/tsd/enforcement assertions and observe expected failure; record exact command and intended diagnostic.
2. Supported-domain tests cover undefined/null/booleans/UTF-16 strings, NaN/infinities/negative zero, sparse arrays and explicit holes, missing versus present-undefined, key-order-independent equality versus order-preserving snapshot transport, frozen detached decoding, and bounded supported prototypes.
3. Explicit negative cases reject cycles/shared references, accessors without invoking getters, hidden properties, user symbols, bigint, data functions, Date/Map/Set/classes, malformed nodes, duplicate/noncanonical keys, and unknown versions. Framework branding is not a generic symbol exemption.
4. Structured property `"0"`, array index 0, and keys containing dots/brackets cannot alias. Supplied value/own/membership/length/keys operations preserve their distinct facts, including inherited presence versus own presence. Selecting a nested path must not traverse unrelated payloads.
5. Independent SHA-256 vectors, including empty text, `abc`, Unicode text, and injected capability behavior, pass against the Node implementation. Runtime Value code imports no Node facilities and passes portable types with `skipLibCheck: false`.
6. Fresh-process canonical roundtrip evidence proves stable bytes and lookup/enumeration meaning, without claiming runtime reuse or durable History publication.
7. Production package participates in API report comparison, declaration views, allowed/forbidden edge fixtures, `npm run check`, `npm test`, and `npm run build`. Missing declaration/gate negative cases fail for the intended reason.

## Delivery

One isolated worktree; claim using delivery conventions, include tests-first evidence, accurate attribution and limitations in the PR template, use `Refs #N`, and stop at PR-open for supervisor review. No publication, paid calls, M3 persistence, or release automation changes. Update the implementation map and focused package documentation; do not rewrite governing normative semantics without the supervisor.

items.title: Explicit subtree output cannot be revalidated and reruns on identical restart
items.body:
## Problem and consumer need

**Medium invalidation precision/performance gap.** A supported memo returning a tracked input subtree republishes on every identical restart:

```ts
run: ({ inputs }) => ({ value: inputs.config.selected })
```

The returned data is correct. The problem is unnecessary execution/publication: a new process with unchanged code and identical inputs reports `unavailable materialized-output at inputs`, while a scalar-only control reuses its exact original result. An unread sibling edit also republishes. For a retained analysis this defeats memoization of ordinary pass-through output.

TRK-5/8 require returned tracked data to count as actual output consumption without including unrelated data. The bounded M3 selected-read decision explicitly retains MDS1 explicit-output observations. REUSE-001 requires checking current bindings and observed inputs; A-01 calls for pass-through changed/unchanged facts. See [Tracking contract](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/blob/c5802daca4a0bb8ea91159854d84eddcfa5215b6/docs/spec/tracking.md) and [acceptance A-01](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/blob/c5802daca4a0bb8ea91159854d84eddcfa5215b6/docs/spec/acceptance.md).

This is a delivered-path validation gap plus a concrete reuse need, not an assertion of a universal obligation to reuse every candidate. It produces conservative misses, not stale accepted output.

## Test-first reproduction

Branch `gap-hunt-contracts`, pinned runner/fixture revision [`4dc00d6af1c2405095792c7be893a1ad2cc382b3`](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/commit/4dc00d6af1c2405095792c7be893a1ad2cc382b3). From a clean checkout with Node24/npm:

```sh
node scratch/gap-hunt/contracts/reproduce.mjs durable-output-minimal
```

The runner installs locked dependencies, builds declarations, compiles and runs only the same-input case plus scalar control. **Observed: 1 failed, 1 passed, 7 skipped.** The retained process reports `published` where `reused` is expected. The supervisor independently reproduced this result; the worker exercised the complete install/build runner. Linux parity awaits the devbox.

[Fixture and independent child process](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/tree/4dc00d6af1c2405095792c7be893a1ad2cc382b3/packages/core/test) are `gap-hunt-contracts-output.test.ts` and `gap-hunt-contracts-output-worker.ts`. [Exact miss evidence](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/blob/4dc00d6af1c2405095792c7be893a1ad2cc382b3/scratch/gap-hunt/contracts/durable-output-misses.log) shows identical MDS1 output bytes and the unavailable current fact.

The broader `durable-output` runner has 8 red/1 green; the component `output` runner has 8 passing shape/precision controls. Some broad rows stop at an early failure, so the full planned rollback assertions are not claimed to have executed. Strict TypeScript and type-aware lint pass.

## Cause and scope

In `packages/resolution/src/current.ts`, `ownFactProvider` handles only `selected` requests for the `inputs` binding before falling through to unavailable. Tracking correctly captured a `materialized-output` request at `config.selected`, but assembled Resolution never supplies that current subtree for comparison. Component Tracking succeeds with a provider that supplies it.

Independent extension at `gap-hunt-dx@a97c11f` now confirms the same missing current-fact handling for **member and forwarded-argument output**, using generated-alpha consumer code and separate processes. The supervisor reran it: **2 failed, 2 passed**. Member subtree output republishes on identical restart (`unavailable materialized-output at member`); its scalar control reuses. A forwarded-argument parent retains its reference by equal-output cutoff, but its child publishes twice (two completed History rows instead of one). That parent result alone would hide the unnecessary child execution. [Extension fixture and commands](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/blob/a97c11f/scratch/gap-hunt/consumer-dx/OUTPUT-BINDINGS.md) preserve the evidence. No stale decoded output is observed. These new fixtures were not included in the owner's older Linux parity bundle.

## Numbered acceptance criteria

1. Identical supported declared-input, member, and forwarded-argument subtree output reuses its exact original result after complete process exit without running/publishing the memo again. Verify the nested child itself, because parent equal-output cutoff can hide an unnecessary child publication.
2. Editing an unread sibling preserves that same exact result.
3. Changed returned leaf, record insertion order, missing/present undefined,
   sparse hole/present undefined, inherited data and inherited/own ownership
   produce the same MDS1 snapshot as independent cold-current computation.
4. Rollback to the original supported input reuses the original exact result.
5. Current output selection resolves only the recorded subtree/address under the
   current binding; do not substitute a stored stale value or widen to whole input.
6. Preserve visible rejection for unsupported Value data, correspondence/scope
   checks and component materialization evidence. Scalar-only controls still reuse.
7. Strict compiler and type-aware lint pass; retain red expectations until fixed.


Scope: current-fact reconstruction for supported input/member/forwarded-argument explicit output, including shape-sensitive MDS1 comparison and precise selected addresses. Do not use JSON equality, stale historical values, whole-input dependencies or unconditional acceptance as a shortcut. No scalar-root expansion, unsupported native/class/accessor support, public API promotion, or release changes.

Blocking dependencies: none. Coordinate shared Resolution/Tracking changes with #155/#162; the owner prioritizes #155's silent false reuse first. This issue does not depend on their fixes. The independently confirmed argument/member reproductions are included here because they expose the same missing current-fact branch.

## Attribution

Implementer: Codex worker (`gpt-6.1-sol`), operating for Mike North.
Agent assistance: The worker authored the cold/current process matrix and traced the missing current-fact branch. Supervising Codex reviewed the contract and consumer boundary, independently reran the minimal failure/control, checked live issues/PRs/labels and filed the gap. No human implementation or review is claimed; no production fix is included.

items.title: Tracked nullable-container guards can silently reuse stale results across restarts
items.body:
## Problem and severity

**High correctness: silent false reuse.** A memo that branches on an ordinary tracked nullable object can return a stale result after the object becomes `null` or its property disappears. The same incorrect reuse survives complete process exit and reopening SQLite. An explicit `!== null` comparison also loses the dependency in the Tracking API.

This requires no untracked closure, mutable global, unsupported value, or code change:

```ts
const declaration = builders.memo({
  subject: 'container-guard',
  run: ({ inputs }) => ({ state: inputs.config.detail ? 'present' : 'absent' }),
});
```

Process A supplies `config.detail = { name: 'Ada' }`. Process B recreates the same declarations against the same store with `detail = null` (or missing), using a fresh request key.

Expected: B publishes `{ state: 'absent' }`.
Observed: B returns `kind: 'reused'` and A's `{ state: 'present' }`.

## Governing contracts

[Tracking TRK-4/5/8](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/blob/c5802daca4a0bb8ea91159854d84eddcfa5215b6/docs/spec/tracking.md) requires tracked branch influences, literal consumed facts, and invalidation when a tracked guard changes. [REUSE-001](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/blob/c5802daca4a0bb8ea91159854d84eddcfa5215b6/docs/spec/execution.md) requires current observed inputs to justify acceptance.

CMP-9 does not promise a JavaScript sandbox, but this probe uses only declared tracked inputs. The separate explicit-null-comparison failure also avoids relying solely on implicit truthiness.

## Minimal failing reproduction

Reproduction branch: `gap-hunt-contracts`, commit [`e580c0751b7b67b6856eb48d04e0046ce7571487`](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/commit/e580c0751b7b67b6856eb48d04e0046ce7571487), over baseline `c5802daca4a0bb8ea91159854d84eddcfa5215b6`.

- [Facade tests](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/blob/e580c0751b7b67b6856eb48d04e0046ce7571487/packages/core/test/gap-hunt-contracts-container-guard.test.ts): reopening in one process and two fully independent processes.
- [Tracking tests](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/blob/e580c0751b7b67b6856eb48d04e0046ce7571487/packages/tracking/test/gap-hunt-contracts-container-guard.test.ts): empty initial container-guard observation set; explicit null comparison; own-presence control.
- [Replay instructions and exact red logs](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/blob/e580c0751b7b67b6856eb48d04e0046ce7571487/scratch/gap-hunt/contracts/README.md).

After `npm ci` and `npm run build`:

```sh
npx tsc -p packages/core/tsconfig.test.json
node --experimental-vm-modules node_modules/jest/bin/jest.js --config packages/core/jest.config.mjs --runInBand --runTestsByPath packages/core/.test-build/test/gap-hunt-contracts-container-guard.test.js
```

Observed independently by the supervising agent on Node 24.22.1: **4 failed, 1 passed**. Both changed-container cases fail in both lifecycle variants; the scalar boolean guard control passes. The low-level worker suite has **3 failed, 1 passed**. Strict TypeScript and type-aware ESLint pass for the probes; no production change is included.

## Suggested direction

Preserve the fact that a navigated field is a container versus a scalar/null/missing value, or enforce an explicit supported observation operation for this case. Do not fix the loss by consuming every nested field: unchanged-container navigation and unread-field precision must remain intact. Cover direct guards, explicit null comparisons, nested navigation, array containers, and independent-process reuse with positive controls.

## Queue handoff

**Pickup-ready implementation contract; first queue priority per owner.**

## Numbered acceptance criteria

1. A normal memo reading `inputs.config.detail ? 'present' : 'absent'` produces the
   correct current value after a record becomes null or an absent property, across
   complete process shutdown. The second result must agree with a separate cold
   current computation. It must never reuse the earlier `present` result.
2. Cover explicit `detail !== null`, `typeof detail` when its result changes, and
   a nullish fallback branch. Record→null, record→missing and reverse transitions
   must be independently tested. Missing and present undefined remain equivalent
   for an ordinary value read under TRK-5.
3. A scalar boolean guard remains a passing control. Nested optional leaf reads
   and record→record replacement with equal consumed leaf values must preserve
   their existing precision and detect later changed current leaves.
4. After a branch changes, current evidence excludes abandoned branch reads.
   Unread sibling/identity edits must not become whole-object dependencies.
5. Add both observer-level operation assertions and assembled durable memo
   assertions using two independent processes, stable declarations, and only
   supported declared input snapshots. A reopened handle alone is insufficient
   process-isolation evidence.
6. The focused strict TypeScript and type-aware lint checks pass. Any unsupported
   builtin diagnostic probes remain explicitly labelled; in particular the
   adversarial `Array.isArray` extension is outside the current documented builtin
   lint allowlist and is not required to expand that allowlist in this issue.

## Scope, exclusions, dependencies

Scope: semantic evidence for supported container/scalar transitions used by ordinary
tracked consumers, and preservation of selected-path precision. No representation
or patch is prescribed. A conservative shape dependency may be acceptable if it
preserves the stated no-whole-payload contract; review that choice explicitly.

Out of scope: arbitrary untracked closure soundness, native reflection support,
new host implementations, package publication, scalar result-root support (#156),
and builtin allowlist expansion. Intrinsic presence overrejection is a separate
candidate root cause, not this issue.

Dependencies: no prerequisite issue is required to reproduce or characterize this
failure. Coordinate with Tracking's no-whole-object navigation invariant and
Resolution's current-fact reconstruction; do not weaken either to silence a test.

## One clean-checkout Linux reproduction command

Run from a clean checkout of branch `gap-hunt-contracts` with Node 24 and npm installed (validated here on 24.22.1). The fixed script revision is recorded in the handoff; the script prints the exact checkout revision before installing pinned dependencies and building all generated declarations:

```sh
node scratch/gap-hunt/contracts/reproduce.mjs 155
```

Expected current result: four intentionally failing container guard assertions,
one passing scalar control. `packages/core/test/gap-hunt-contracts-guard-worker.ts`
is part of the same commit and supplies the independent-process reproduction.
No paid provider or external service is involved. The broader operation oracle is
`gap-hunt-contracts-operation-matrix.test.ts` (six red, seven green).

Fixed reproduction revision: `9267a44e1a203966e6ccd73db188e5826506326b` on branch `gap-hunt-contracts`.
The script and all required fixture modules are present in that commit.

## Attribution

Implementer: Codex worker (`gpt-6.1-sol`), operating for Mike North.
Agent assistance: The worker authored and ran the tests. The supervising Codex agent reviewed the contract and fixture, independently reran the facade reproduction, checked existing issues, and filed this finding. No human implementation or review is claimed.

items.title: M3: Prove and implement nested selected result materialization
items.body:
## Outcome and governing contracts

Close the scalar-only M2 gap for ordinary retained activity.profile.name and indexed PR/review loops without loading unread source payload. Establish the bounded synchronous nested-reading contract and its SQL address-index evidence before durable History depends on it.

Requirements: DOM-2/3, TRK-1/2/5, VAL-1/2, RES-002/003, PKG boundaries; docs/plans/m3-contribution-analysis.md.

Dependencies: #51 (plan), #52 (actual SQLite capability for restart selection proof).

Acceptance:
1. Read/reconcile the existing History scalar read port, Tracking materialization bridge and Value MDS1/MDO1 contracts. Add a separate alpha exact navigation capability returning tagged scalar fact/record/array shape. Never put fabricated shape objects inside ISelectedFact.fact. Container navigation is not a whole-object observation; leaf, length, presence and key-order retain existing semantics.

M2 needs selected stored-value access connected to semantic observation contracts, without promoting the EXP-2 prototype into a persistence/runtime product. Depends on #24 and #26. Stay backlog until their alpha ports are accepted.

Consume an injected selected reader and observation sink, never private rows/frames. Any History-owned exact-reader port must be introduced with tests and approved by the supervisor; no durable backend implementation or publication in this issue.

Selected loading supports the EXP-2 synchronous indexed top-level scalar domain: unexpected scalar field reads load exactly that field and record it. Fingerprint metadata comparison loads no payload. Unsupported nested lazy, presence/enumeration/prototype and async-only unexpected getter operations fail explicitly, never fabricate a fact. Explicit async preparation can be shown only with its bounded limitations; it cannot be presented as a general ordinary-getter solution.

Output materialization must record selected output facts and return detached immutable supported data. Integrate the Tracking pass-through case: returning tracked input as data consumes the data actually materialized, without treating unrelated reachable data as output. items.title: Repeated array validation makes structured result publication quadratic
items.body:
## Problem and severity

**High scale/performance gap.** Publishing a supported flat array repeatedly validates the entire root array while constructing selected-address evidence. Doubling record count nearly quadruples validation work and publication time. A synthetic 11.24 MB result took about 155 seconds to publish on the tested host.

History's [buildIndex/addAddress](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/blob/c5802daca4a0bb8ea91159854d84eddcfa5215b6/packages/history/src/durable/selected-index.ts#L187) calls `observe(root, address, 'value')` for each address. Value's [assertArraySurface](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/blob/c5802daca4a0bb8ea91159854d84eddcfa5215b6/packages/value/src/value.ts#L238) enumerates and validates all root slots on those paths. The CPU profile's dominant sampled frame is `assertArraySurface`.

## Governing consumer need

The contribution pipeline needs to process tens of thousands of PRs/reviews and retain multi-megabyte results. DOM-3 requires the same semantic model for enormous source datasets; TEST-5/A-17 require measured scale and bounded materialization evidence. M7 scale is explicitly undelivered, so this finding identifies a concrete current bottleneck rather than asserting a shipped latency SLA.

## Minimal deterministic failing reproduction

Branch `gap-hunt-dx`, commit [`b3cb37922691005193d38a7479e1239938896da4`](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/commit/b3cb37922691005193d38a7479e1239938896da4): [array-validation.test.ts](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/blob/b3cb37922691005193d38a7479e1239938896da4/packages/core/test/gap-hunt-scale/array-validation.test.ts).

After `npm ci` and `npm run build`:

```sh
npx tsc -p packages/core/tsconfig.test.json
node --experimental-vm-modules node_modules/jest/bin/jest.js --config packages/core/jest.config.mjs --runInBand --runTestsByPath packages/core/.test-build/test/gap-hunt-scale/array-validation.test.js
```

The test observes array-slot enumeration without changing native reflection results, using real SQLite stage/publication and the same payload for an encoding-only control:

| Records | Matched encoding slot work | Stage/publication slot work |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 20 | 20 | 1,323 |
| 40 | 40 | 5,043 |

The proposed regression boundary is linear validation work for this fixed flat shape: doubling records should at most double inspected slots. Actual work exceeds the 2,646 bound with 5,043. The supervisor independently reproduced the exact failure. This is a deterministic count, not a timing assertion or a universal complexity proof. Strict TypeScript and repository type-aware lint pass.

## Measured workload

Node 24.22.1, macOS arm64; fresh synthetic arrays of records with a 512-byte body:

| Records | JSON bytes | SQLite bytes after close | Publication, approximate | Matched encoding |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1,000 | 558,781 | 3,190,784 | 361 ms | 2.10 ms |
| 2,000 | 1,119,781 | 6,250,496 | 1,251 ms | 2.52 ms |
| 4,000 | 2,241,781 | 12,345,344 | 4,979 ms | 4.00 ms |
| 20,000 | 11,237,781 | 61,779,968 | 155,544 ms | not sampled in this run |

[Benchmark source, corrected results and replay commands](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/tree/b3cb37922691005193d38a7479e1239938896da4/scratch/gap-hunt/scale) include CPU-profile regeneration. Wall time varies with machine load; the deterministic small counterexample and hot-path profile support the diagnosis independently. The approximately 5.5x store amplification is measured context, not a separate assertion that required selected-read indexes are wrong or that this fixture reproduces a reported 14.6x consumer ratio.

## Suggested direction

Validate the immutable supported payload once at the trusted boundary, then construct selected-address evidence without revalidating the whole root at every address. Preserve rejection of unsupported arrays/prototypes/accessors, exact canonical selected facts, and lazy-read correctness. Retain the operation-count regression probe and rerun matched payload benchmarks. Do not trade away fail-closed Value validation for speed.

## Implementation contract and queue handoff

Pickup-ready within the scope below; workflow labels remain the supervisor's responsibility.

Governing need: DOM-3 and TEST-5. History selected indexing repeatedly calls Value observe at each address; the root array's full supported surface is scanned each time. One bounded regression at20/40records measures array-slot validation work, avoiding scheduler/latency assumptions.

```sh
node scratch/gap-hunt/contract-surface/repro-160.mjs
```

1. Supported flat record-array publication avoids a whole-root scan for each selected address; doubled fixture work stays within the proposed linear bound while matched encoding control remains linear.
2. Exact root and selected nested values/fingerprints after publication match independently encoded observations, including sparse slots, undefined, -0/NaN and explicit array length where supported.
3. Unsupported accessors, cycles/shared references, symbols and malformed array surfaces still reject before completed publication. A validation cache must not admit mutation or unsupported values by accident.
4. Selected fingerprint comparisons still avoid loading root/unrelated payload; exact retained references and atomic publication remain unchanged.
5. Broaden the work counter to flat/nested records and multiple independent payloads so a per-process stale-validation cache cannot falsely pass.

Scope: validated immutable payload/index construction and owner contract tests. Do not remove selected indexes, weaken supported-value checks, introduce fake progress/lease renewals or promise fixed throughput. Keep Machine/Value/History ownership and injected ports. Storage amplification and100k capacity are measured separately; a VACUUM/compaction policy is not required by this finding.

items.title: Presence checks on supported plain records reject intrinsic property names
items.body:
## Problem and governing contract

**Medium correctness: valid presence operations are rejected.** On a supported ordinary `{}`, own-presence checks for `constructor`, `__proto__`, `toString`, and `hasOwnProperty` should return false; inherited membership should return true. Both currently throw `Unsupported value ... intrinsic inherited data`. Ordinary tracked `'constructor' in input` fails too.

TRK-5 in [tracking.md](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/blob/c5802daca4a0bb8ea91159854d84eddcfa5215b6/docs/spec/tracking.md#observation-decision-table) says own checks consume ownership only and `in` consumes presence, neither the value at that key. The selected Value domain permits plain-data prototype chains ending in `Object.prototype` and rejects selected intrinsic **values**. This reproduction requests presence, so no native function/accessor serialization is needed.

The cause is `observeAt` calling `lookupValidated` before branching on own/membership/value in `packages/value/src/value.ts`. The intrinsic-value restriction is applied even when only a boolean fact is consumed. This is distinct from #155's omitted container-guard dependency.

## Test-first reproduction

Branch `gap-hunt-contracts`, fixed reproduction commit [`9267a44e1a203966e6ccd73db188e5826506326b`](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/commit/9267a44e1a203966e6ccd73db188e5826506326b), baseline `c5802daca4a0bb8ea91159854d84eddcfa5215b6`.

From a clean checkout of that revision with Node24 and npm:

```sh
node scratch/gap-hunt/contracts/reproduce.mjs intrinsic
```

The runner installs locked dependencies, builds generated declarations, compiles and runs [the focused fixture](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/blob/9267a44e1a203966e6ccd73db188e5826506326b/packages/tracking/test/gap-hunt-contracts-intrinsic-presence.test.ts). No local absolute paths, existing stores or paid services are required. Linux execution is pending the owner's devbox; the command uses portable Node/npm entrypoints.

Observed: **9 failed, 2 passed**, independently rerun by the supervising agent on Node24.22.1/macOS. All eight special-name own/membership assertions and ordinary tracked membership fail. Selected intrinsic-value rejection and supported shadowing/custom plain-data prototype controls pass. Strict TypeScript and type-aware lint pass. The script propagates the red suite's nonzero status.

## Implementation handoff

Pickup-ready within the existing supported domain. Queue priority follows #155's silent false reuse and precedes DX/docs. Start by retaining the observed failing presence assertions.

## Numbered acceptance criteria

1. For a supported ordinary `{}`, own-presence of `constructor`, `__proto__`,
   `toString`, and `hasOwnProperty` returns false; inherited membership returns
   true. Both operations record only their boolean semantic fact and structured
   address, without evaluating or encoding the intrinsic member's value.
2. Ordinary tracked `'constructor' in input` succeeds and records one membership
   observation. The owning explicit own-property helper agrees with Value's own
   observation. Do not implement membership as an own-only check.
3. Transition an own supported data property to inherited intrinsic presence:
   own-presence changes true→false, while inherited membership remains true.
   Unrelated sibling edits do not alter those facts; deletion under a null-ending
   chain produces the actual absent membership result.
4. Selected intrinsic **value** reads continue to reject explicitly; this issue
   must not add native function/accessor data support. Preserve rejection of user
   accessors without invoking them, unsupported class/native prototypes, and
   prototype-depth violations. Preserve supported custom plain-data prototypes
   and own-data shadowing of intrinsic names.
5. Assertions cover Value and Tracking, include positive/negative controls,
   and pass strict TypeScript and type-aware lint. Add current-fact comparison
   or assembled durable acceptance coverage so this is not merely a direct lookup
   special case. No discarded or fabricated dependency fact is acceptable.

Scope: operation-specific presence semantics within the already selected supported
plain-data prototype domain. Out of scope: #155 container evidence, arbitrary
prototype/native data support, native reflection as an alternative observation
API, provider work or publication. No design-policy expansion is required.


Dependencies: no blocking issue. Coordinate shared Value/Tracking edits with #155 if concurrently claimed, but this reproduction and correction do not depend on its resolution.

## Attribution

Implementer: Codex worker (`gpt-6.1-sol`), operating for Mike North.
Agent assistance: The worker authored the synthetic reproduction and contract. The supervising Codex agent inspected TRK-5 and the supported prototype boundary, independently reran the 9-red/2-green fixture, checked live issues/PRs/labels, and filed this finding. No human implementation or review is claimed. No production fix is included.

items.title: Tracked nullable-container guards can silently reuse stale results across restarts
items.body:
## Problem and severity

**High correctness: silent false reuse.** A memo that branches on an ordinary tracked nullable object can return a stale result after the object becomes `null` or its property disappears. The same incorrect reuse survives complete process exit and reopening SQLite. An explicit `!== null` comparison also loses the dependency in the Tracking API.

This requires no untracked closure, mutable global, unsupported value, or code change:

```ts
const declaration = builders.memo({
  subject: 'container-guard',
  run: ({ inputs }) => ({ state: inputs.config.detail ? 'present' : 'absent' }),
});
```

Process A supplies `config.detail = { name: 'Ada' }`. Process B recreates the same declarations against the same store with `detail = null` (or missing), using a fresh request key.

Expected: B publishes `{ state: 'absent' }`.
Observed: B returns `kind: 'reused'` and A's `{ state: 'present' }`.

## Governing contracts

[Tracking TRK-4/5/8](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/blob/c5802daca4a0bb8ea91159854d84eddcfa5215b6/docs/spec/tracking.md) requires tracked branch influences, literal consumed facts, and invalidation when a tracked guard changes. [REUSE-001](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/blob/c5802daca4a0bb8ea91159854d84eddcfa5215b6/docs/spec/execution.md) requires current observed inputs to justify acceptance.

CMP-9 does not promise a JavaScript sandbox, but this probe uses only declared tracked inputs. The separate explicit-null-comparison failure also avoids relying solely on implicit truthiness.

## Minimal failing reproduction

Reproduction branch: `gap-hunt-contracts`, commit [`e580c0751b7b67b6856eb48d04e0046ce7571487`](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/commit/e580c0751b7b67b6856eb48d04e0046ce7571487), over baseline `c5802daca4a0bb8ea91159854d84eddcfa5215b6`.

Preserve the fact that a navigated field is a container versus a scalar/null/missing value, or enforce an explicit supported observation operation for this case. Do not fix the loss by consuming every nested field: unchanged-container navigation and unread-field precision must remain intact. Cover direct guards, explicit null comparisons, nested navigation, array containers, and independent-process reuse with positive controls.

   a nullish fallback branch. Record→null, record→missing and reverse transitions

3. A scalar boolean guard remains a passing control. Nested optional leaf reads
   and record→record replacement with equal consumed leaf values must preserve
   their existing precision and detect later changed current leaves.
4. After a branch changes, current evidence excludes abandoned branch reads.
   Unread sibling/identity edits must not become whole-object dependencies.
5. Add both observer-level operation assertions and assembled durable memo
   assertions using two independent processes, stable declarations, and only
   supported declared input snapshots. A reopened handle alone is insufficient
   process-isolation evidence.
6. The focused strict TypeScript and type-aware lint checks pass. Any unsupported
   builtin diagnostic probes remain explicitly labelled; in particular the
   adversarial `Array.isArray` extension is outside the current documented builtin
   lint allowlist and is not required to expand that allowlist in this issue.

## Scope, exclusions, dependencies

Scope: semantic evidence for supported container/scalar transitions used by ordinary
tracked consumers, and preservation of selected-path precision. No representation
or patch is prescribed. A conservative shape dependency may be acceptable if it
preserves the stated no-whole-payload contract; review that choice explicitly.

Out of scope: arbitrary untracked closure soundness, native reflection support,
new host implementations, package publication, scalar result-root support (#156),
and builtin allowlist expansion. Intrinsic presence overrejection is a separate
candidate root cause, not this issue.

failure. Coordinate with Tracking's no-whole-object navigation invariant and

items.title: Alpha authoring accepts scalar result types that execution rejects
items.body:
## Problem and severity

**Medium API/DX inconsistency.** The alpha authoring types accept a source or memo whose result is a string, number, boolean, null, or undefined. Execution rejects all five with `unsupported-result` after the body has run. Returning a record containing the same atom succeeds.

For example, both of these declarations typecheck:

```ts
const memo = builders.memo({ subject: 'scalar-memo', run: () => 'ready' });
const source = builders.source<string>({
  subject: 'scalar-source',
  run: ({ outcome }) => outcome.fresh('ready'),
});
```

Resolving either produces `ResolutionError: Step [...] produced a result without a record or array root`. This matters when a consumer memoizes a serialized dependency or a scalar calculation: the author learns the root restriction only after doing the work.

## Governing contract and interpretation

VAL-2 supports these atoms as values. CMP-8 explicitly distinguishes skipped/no-value from success returning undefined. The generated `source<TResult>` and `memo<TResult>` declarations do not restrict `TResult` to record/array roots, and the facade authoring guide does not state that restriction.

However, the M3 nested selected-navigation decision is expressly bounded to record and array roots. The owner selected the bounded resolution on 2026-10-22: **enforce record/array roots for current alpha and document wrappers**. Scalar-root runtime support is outside this issue.

Expected after the selected fix: generated alpha authoring declarations reject bare scalar roots and document `{ value }` wrappers before execution. Observed: all ten atom source/memo cases compile, then fail during result publication; five record-wrapped controls succeed.

## Minimal failing reproduction

Branch `gap-hunt-contracts`, commit [`110d825832e754bf7426027f2242edf68e3000d9`](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/commit/110d825832e754bf7426027f2242edf68e3000d9), over baseline `c5802daca4a0bb8ea91159854d84eddcfa5215b6`.

- [Generated-alpha tsd acceptance](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/blob/110d825832e754bf7426027f2242edf68e3000d9/packages/core/test-d/gap-hunt-contracts-scalar-roots.test-d.ts).
- [Exact commands and logs](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/blob/110d825832e754bf7426027f2242edf68e3000d9/scratch/gap-hunt/contracts/SCALAR-ROOTS.md).

After `npm ci` and `npm run build`:

```sh
npx tsc -p packages/core/tsconfig.test.json
npm run test:types --workspace microdelta
node --experimental-vm-modules node_modules/jest/bin/jest.js --config packages/core/jest.config.mjs --runInBand --runTestsByPath packages/core/.test-build/test/gap-hunt-contracts-scalar-roots.test.js
```

The supervising agent independently reran the string source/memo and wrapped-string control: **2 failures, 1 pass**. Synthetic fresh stores isolate every case. No production changes.

## Owner decision and implementation contract

**Pickup-ready. Owner decision (2026-10-22): enforce record/array roots for current alpha; document wrappers.** No scalar-root runtime expansion is authorized by this issue. This resolves the earlier provisional choice.

### Numbered acceptance criteria

1. Make the existing record/array result-root boundary explicit in current-alpha authoring types and facade documentation, linked to the bounded M3 contract. Show a complete supported `{ value }` wrapper example for a scalar calculation or serialized dependency.
2. Generated-alpha tsd negative tests reject bare string, number, boolean, null and undefined roots from both `source` and `memo`, including inferred and explicit generic authoring forms. Write and observe these negative-type tests fail against the reproduction baseline before implementation.
3. Preserve valid record and readonly-array inference, named record interfaces, and declaration-tier/package boundaries. The existing record-wrapped controls must still execute successfully; do not broaden accepted class/native/function data to satisfy a type constraint.
4. Untyped JavaScript or deliberately invalid inputs continue to fail visibly at the runtime supported-result boundary, publish no completed result, and retain the actionable `unsupported-result` diagnostic. Type constraints do not replace runtime validation.
5. Supported nested scalar fields—including present undefined and the selected Value numeric domain—keep their semantics. Skipped/no-value remains distinct from a successful record containing an undefined field.
6. Strict TypeScript, generated-declaration tsd, type-aware lint, valid runtime controls and workspace declaration checks pass. Convert the existing scalar-root runtime matrix to assertions of the selected rejection contract; do not make unsupported scalar execution succeed to turn the old diagnostic matrix green.

items.title: Allow explicit custom keys for collection members without a designated string identity
items.body:
## Finding and severity

**Medium correctness/DX:** the current private-alpha template rejects an explicit supported custom string key unless the source also declares a designated string identity. COL-1 and CMP-4 permit the custom-key alternative, including member schemas without such an identity field. This is a scoped authoring gap; no runtime or type-contract expansion to unsupported values is requested.

## Governing intent and delivery boundary

COL-1 (`docs/spec/tracking.md:227–232`) allows an explicit author custom-key function; “No-identity members need an explicit supported key strategy before keyed work proceeds.” CMP-4 (`docs/spec/composition.md:54–57`) requires keying before any gate/member work using designated identity **or** an explicit custom key. `docs/plans/m4-composition.md:143–150` repeats the alternative and pre-work validation. The key remains a nonempty string scoped to its collection; this candidate does not ask to admit numeric keys, ordinals or implicit fallback.

The selected M4 and EXP-4 fixtures already have string designated identities (M4 plan79–82; EXP-4 decision23–32). Their custom-key variants replace one string field with another. Current tests `packages/core/test/keyed/restart.test.ts:249–270` establish correspondence under renumbered designated IDs, not authoring of no-string-identity schemas. Implementation comments call a custom key an override of designated identity. The supervisor independently reproduced the gap and accepted the explicit-custom-key alternative as settled intent. The narrower fixtures do not require unused identity fields; do not claim those existing fixtures failed or that arbitrary collection types were promised.

## Minimal measured reproduction

Members are supported records `{id:7,score:3}`. Generated-alpha code declares a source of `{status:'complete',members:[...]}` and a template custom key `member => 'id:'+member.id`. It typechecks without casts/suppressions, then `api.template` throws `DefinitionError`: `Template member must fan out over a keyed collection source declaring its designated identity.` `template.ts:403–406` checks the required source marker before considering the key.

The numeric-only schema cannot supply that marker through current types: `ICollectionOptions` requires `identity` and `IIdentityField` admits only string-valued member fields. `collection:{}` and `identity:'id'` both fail generated-alpha type tests. Adding only optional `key?:string` to the TypeScript member interface, plus the identity marker, makes identical physical data and custom key execute successfully: discovery key `id:7`, member succeeded. This fictional annotation is a diagnostic workaround, not proposed caller syntax.

Current minimal runtime outcome: **one red/two green**. Explicit custom string key without fictional identity is rejected (red); no key strategy is rejected (green); optional identity annotation plus custom key completes actual member work (green). Type/lint checks pass. Existing AUTHORING-MATRIX.md records the broader passing arrays/source-envelope/gate controls.

From a clean checkout of `gap-hunt-dx` at [`b1b42c304db15fe0c3c306a0fb4f71660970040f`](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/commit/b1b42c304db15fe0c3c306a0fb4f71660970040f), with Node24.x/npm on PATH:

```sh
node scratch/gap-hunt/consumer-dx/repro-custom-key.mjs
```

Default runner installs locked dependencies, builds all package declarations, strictly compiles only the custom-key fixture, checks it with repository type-aware ESLint, then runs the three assertions. Native better-sqlite3 prerequisites are the same as the repository; no global CLI, credentials or provider execution is needed. Validated from detached clean worktree98c70b8: default npmci/build:packages, focused strict compile and type-aware lint all passed, then the intended one-red/two-green runtime assertions produced exit1 (`logs/custom-key-clean-bootstrap.log`). The final Jest runner at b1b42c3 was then executed against a fresh package build: strict compiler/lint passed and Jest reported one red/two green (`logs/custom-key-jest.log`); the supervisor independently repeated that Jest result. Full default bootstrap at the final Jest revision has not been rerun. Baseline expected exit1 is the intended acceptance failure. `GAP_HUNT_REUSE_BUILD=1` skips bootstrap only when dependencies and generated package outputs are already fresh. No command depends on a user-specific path.

## Numbered acceptance criteria

1. A caller can declare a supported collection whose member schema has no designated string-valued identity field, supply an explicit custom function returning supported nonempty string keys, and execute keyed member work. Do not require a fictional identity field, additional payload projection, or a cast/suppression solely to satisfy declaration machinery. No particular field name or constructor spelling is prescribed.
2. The generated alpha contract accepts that supported path with precise member fields in the key/gate/member bodies. Unsupported key return types and mismatched collection result types produce appropriate diagnostics; generated consumer checks use built alpha outputs. Do not loosen unrelated type checks or admit arbitrary native values.
3. Default designated-identity behavior remains supported. Missing designated identity with no custom strategy is rejected before gate/member execution, with a diagnostic naming the collection and key strategy. No ordinal/index/label fallback is introduced.
4. Custom key validation remains pre-work and whole-snapshot: duplicate keys, absent/undefined return, empty string, non-string return and a thrown key function yield the appropriate rejection/diagnostic and admit no gate/member body. Deliberately invalid runtime returns may be exercised from JavaScript without weakening production TypeScript checks.
5. Stable custom keys retain correspondence and exact eligible member references across process exit and source reorder. When a caller changes its key strategy's output for a member (an unstable or changed key), it must not guess correspondence or silently reuse the prior instance under the new key; normal new-key correspondence applies. Duplicate results from an unstable strategy still reject. This does not require proving arbitrary key functions deterministic or detecting hidden closure state.
6. Preserve collection scoping and preexisting default/custom identity tests, gate behavior and frozen topology. Identity is author-declared policy; the implementation must not infer a default from numeric id, record position or payload equality.
7. The minimal baseline reproduction becomes green through the accepted contract path, while both controls stay green. Add focused type/runtime negative tests and separate-process custom-key controls derived from these outcomes before changing implementation; check strict TypeScript, type-aware lint, API reports/declaration consumers and affected Definition/assembly tests.

## Scope, owners and dependencies

Definition & Binding owns collection declaration, key strategy and symbolic template typing. Reuse Resolution consumes keyed snapshots/correspondence; the facade aliases the generated contracts. Change only the owning source/template contracts, generated declarations/API reports and focused tests/docs needed for this path. No new host capability, persistence format/schema, paid-provider behavior, release tier, package publication or general CLI is required. Runtime authority stays with existing owners.

No prerequisite production fix is known. Coordinate generated facade aliases with producer builds; use a fresh isolated issue worktree if authorized. The supervisor classified this as a scoped authoring gap; no new product policy decision is required. Do not require a new collection field/API spelling solely because this fixture used an omitted marker to expose the mismatch.

## Attribution

Agent assistance: Supervising Codex reviewed the governing clauses and implementation, independently reproduced one failed acceptance and two passing controls, checked live issues/PRs/labels, and filed the issue. No human implementation or review is claimed.

items.body:
**Medium authoring/DX correctness.** A supported asynchronous source check works at runtime but is rejected by the generated private-alpha authoring declarations.

## Consumer contract and classification

Current source authoring should permit a check/retrieval callback to await work before returning its trusted fresh/retain outcome. `docs/spec/execution.md` REUSE-004 describes a conditional request confirming unchanged data and retaining the previous exact snapshot, with the work recorded separately. M5 operational work is scoped to the invocation lifetime. This need exists for an ordinary source today and does not depend on future M7 pagination.

This is a scoped **declaration gap**: strict generated-alpha TypeScript rejects `async ({ outcome }) => outcome.fresh<IValue>({ value: 1 })` and async conditional retain, although JavaScript runtime controls execute those outcomes correctly. No synchronous-source boundary was found in active M3/M4/M5 plans. Their synchronous restrictions concern SQLite/selected materialization getters. The sync/async implementation-choice sentence at execution.md:187 refers to finality hooks; it does not require source check/retrieval to be synchronous.

`async-source.ts` imports only the facade API with the required generated owner-declaration mappings. Matching synchronous fresh/retain controls compile. Four async callbacks fail with **TS2322**: direct source fresh/retain and template-member source fresh/retain. Every payload is the supported object `{ value: 1 }`; no cast, suppression or weakened compiler setting is used.

The restrictive signatures are `packages/definition/src/declaration.ts:230` (`ISourceOptions.run`) and `packages/definition/src/template.ts:90` (`ITemplateSourceOptions.run`), both returning only `IApply<TFamily['outcomes'], TResult>`. items.title: Author-created ResolutionError bypasses safe memo failure messages
items.body:
## Problem and governing contract

**Medium correctness/privacy gap:** an author-created `ResolutionError` with a non-`execution-failure` code escapes the memo body's failure wrapper. Its author-selected text becomes the outer framework message, and the original object is not preserved as that wrapper's cause.

[RUN-013](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/blob/2a640aca75d5728484a2cb06af88c77690616ba9/docs/spec/operations.md#run-013--retry-history-is-part-of-supervision) says framework failure messages identify the step/position and failure kind only: “What author or caller code throws ... never enters them.” The exported ResolutionError contract repeats that boundary. It makes no exception for author-created instances of an exported error class.

This is a distinct recurrence after closed #147, which repaired ordinary author Error interpolation. Its ordinary-Error control still passes. Owning area: Resolution's memo failure boundary, consumed through Core's alpha authoring/workspace facade. Genuine declared-child runtime failures must keep their existing classification.

## Failing reproduction and exact observation

Published evidence: [`gap-hunt-error-privacy@49c47b79346e78ae9ef22f8985d254254200a14c`](https://github.com/mike-north/microdelta/blob/49c47b79346e78ae9ef22f8985d254254200a14c/scratch/gap-hunt/error-privacy/REPORT.md). The exact clean execution was at `702a15f56f69884f449dd6cfbd31c9b7420f06ec`; the final commit adds captures/report/contract only, with runner, fixture and runtime byte-identical. From a clean checkout with Node24/npm and native SQLite prerequisites:

```sh
python3 scratch/gap-hunt/error-privacy/run.py
```

The command installs/builds, compiles strictly, runs type-aware lint and checks the exact expected negative oracle. Its exit0 means the reproduction succeeded, **not** that the product assertions are green. Test: `packages/core/test/gap-hunt-error-privacy.test.ts`.

A bound author helper throws `new ResolutionError('unsupported-result', 'SYNTHETIC-OPAQUE-DETAIL-9d72')`. Before the assertion, the actual facade result records:

- outer code: `unsupported-result`, expected safe author-failure classification;
- outer message: exactly the synthetic marker, expected a safe message naming the step;
- outer error is the thrown object: true; outer cause is the thrown object: false;
- no completed result is returned.

The message assertion fails. The later expected code/cause assertions do not execute; their observed values above are recorded separately before that failure. The run has8 passing tests,1 intended failure,0 runtime-error suites. Strict compile and lint pass. A fresh independent checkout ran the complete default command with clean tracked source before/after.

The confirmed discrepancy is the outer framework message/cause boundary. No author-path event or store leakage, sandbox escape, or failure of every callback path is claimed. Six separate opaque provider-error cases do pass their event/diagnostic/store checks.

## Numbered acceptance criteria

1. An author memo body/helper throwing a constructed exported ResolutionError with a non-execution-failure code receives a safe `execution-failure` outer message naming the step, with the exact thrown object preserved as cause. Author-selected text must not become the outer framework message. Cover the reproduced code and another non-execution-failure code; class identity alone is not evidence that the runtime originated a failure.
2. Preserve ordinary author Error and author-created execution-failure wrapping/cause identity. Observe the new non-execution-failure case fail before implementation while the ordinary-Error control remains green; after implementation all these cases pass as ordinary assertions.
3. A real declared child returning unsupported data still propagates the existing runtime `unsupported-result` classification and safe message. A parent that swallows a failed child must still not publish an incomplete successful result. Do not fix the author case by discarding genuine child failure semantics.
4. Preserve the six bounded provider controls: explicit failed response versus unknown rejected-perform semantics, independent sibling progress, exactly one provider invocation, opaque cause identity on the returned failure path, and no conversion/getter evaluation or synthetic detail in event/diagnostic/store views.
5. The original nine-case fixture becomes all-green regression coverage. Retain strict TypeScript, type-aware lint, declaration boundaries and the repository's required checks. Record the test-first result and exact commands/current-head outcome in the PR; do not keep the expected-red evidence runner as a passing product CI gate.

## Scope, exclusions and dependencies

Scope: the memo-body author failure boundary, its provenance distinction from genuine runtime child failures, and focused regression tests. Suggested direction: preserve that provenance distinction instead of trusting the public error class or message contents. The issue does not prescribe a representation.

Out of scope: a new error API, redacting deliberate caller access to `cause`, changing genuine child classifications, new hosts/provider integrations, hostile-JavaScript sandboxing, scalar result support, paid-provider calls, package publication or releases. items.title: M2: Capture branded tracked values and current semantic observations
items.body:
## Problem and scope

Production Tracking currently captures process-local tags only. M2 requires ordinary object reads and function calls to produce portable semantic evidence while retaining isolated capture and reactive composition.

Governing contracts: TRK-1 through TRK-8, VAL-1/2/3, ARC-001 through ARC-004, A-01/A-04/A-15/A-18. Depends on #24. This issue remains backlog until Value declarations are accepted and the supervisor records the bounded object-ownership/update and alpha API contracts here.

## Intended behavior and ownership

- Transparent nominally branded `tracked()` supports the selected plain-object/array domain and normal function invocation, rejects primitive wrapper inputs in types and runtime, and allows importing a tracked declaration without rewrapping at each consumer.
- Tracking captures operations and compares supplied current facts. Definition/composition supplies current binding correspondence; Tracking must not derive restart identity from function text, labels, object identity, or invocation order. Any binding descriptor supplied to Tracking is copied/validated and treated as caller-owned correspondence information, not a Tracking registry's proof of identity.
- Called tracked functions contribute automatic actual-called implementation evidence and internal tracked reads/calls, but are not memoized merely by wrapping. Uncalled functions contribute no code dependency. Document emitted-build-artifact invalidation policy and closure limits. Use the injected hash/async-context capabilities without direct Node access.
- Capture sync/async operations in isolated frames, restore surrounding context on success/throw/rejection, fail clearly on detached late use, and replay observations through cached local derivations. Keep tag/revision/frame state process-local; only immutable versioned semantic evidence leaves the persistence-facing seam.
- Controlled state changes and ownership must prevent a cached derivation from silently reusing evidence after an unobservable mutation. The supervisor will record the concrete minimal contract before implementation; do not silently choose raw mutable inputs with unverifiable cache validity.

## Tests first and acceptance

1. Jest and tsd failures before implementation: supported wrappers and primitive/class rejection, nominal brand and normal call/return typing, imported declarations, and intentional alpha/default-public declaration boundaries.
2. TRK-5 local supported operations: leaf reads without whole-object/identity inflation; missing vs present-undefined; actual falsey guard values; own versus inherited presence; key enumeration/order without member payload reads; array length and positional paths; explicit identity-field reads; pass-through argument reads only as consumed by the callee. Reflection must preserve Proxy invariants and must not accidentally record stronger dependencies than the performed operation.
3. Actual-called implementation evidence, uncalled helper exclusion, repeated calls execute repeatedly, tracked nested/async function reads, and bounded unsupported function/native behavior with diagnostics.
4. Changed branch replaces abandoned reads; concurrent frames remain isolated; nested throw/rejection restores parent; detached work after close rejects; cached derived success/failure replays relevant semantic evidence without storing tags.
5. A-04 M2 slice uses an injected current-fact/binding provider: replace author A with B keeping the name equal, then change B's name. First selected-fact comparison equals, second changes; original observation snapshot remains immutable. Missing/ambiguous correspondence yields an explicit non-equal/unavailable result, never guessed remapping. Durable accepted result references and persisted provenance remain M3.
6. Selected output/pass-through materialization integrates through an observation contract with the dependent M2 materialization issue; no returned tracked object can be treated as a fully observed immutable snapshot merely because it crossed a function boundary.
7. Tests and generated declarations demonstrate immutable serializable evidence with no live tags, revisions, closures, or mutable source objects. Required check/test/build and import/declaration boundaries pass.

## Delivery and exclusions

One isolated worktree and issue claim; accurate PR template with test-first evidence and `Refs #N`; stop at PR-open. No History writes, reuse eligibility/source policy, graph mutation or general fanout. No claim of arbitrary JavaScript closure soundness. Normative changes require supervisor review.
